Part 1: What is Software Engineering?

Pentium Example

Source: wikimedia

Pentium division bug

  • 1 in 9 billion divisions were affected
  • Thomas Nicely (a math professor) found it while computing with prime numbers
  • The results didn’t agree with theory

Ariane 5 Example

European Space Agency

  • In the 1990s, self-destructed 37 seconds after its first launch
  • The Ariane 5’s guidance software was reused from the Ariane 4

Source: wikimedia

Ariane 5 Example

Source: wikipedia

  • Overflow: Velocity calculation converted from double (64 bits) to short (16 bits)
  • Exception handler had been disabled for efficiency reasons
  • The cost of the failure was $1 billion

Hacking vs. Engineering

Hacking

🙈 writing lots of code before testing any of it

🙈 keeping all the details in your head

🙈 assuming that bugs won’t exist

Software engineering

😎 write a little bit at a time, testing as you go

😎 document your assumptions

😎 defend your code against yourself

Topics in Software Engineering

  • Testing and linting (unit tests, today)
  • Debugging (coverage, today)
  • Version control (GitHub)
  • Code review (GitHub pull request)
  • Continuous integration (GitHub actions)
  • Refactoring
  • Design patterns

Part 2: Unit Tests

Validation

Testing ⊂ validation and includes:

  • Verification: Formal proof that a program is correct
  • Code review: Somebody else reads your code
  • Testing: Run on selected inputs and check results

Some Stats

Quality Level Defects / kloc Example
typical industry software 1–10 most commercial software
high-quality validation 0.1–1 Java libraries
safety-critical validation 0.01–0.1 NASA
  • kloc: one thousand lines of source code

Why Are There So Many Bugs?

  • Exhaustive testing not possible: too many test cases
  • Example: multiply two numbers a x b

Why Are There So Many Bugs?

  • 1-bit numbers:
a × b b = 0 b = 1
a = 0 0 0
a = 1 0 1

Why Are There So Many Bugs?

  • 2-bit numbers:
a × b b = 0 b = 1 b = 2 b = 3
a = 0 0 0 0 0
a = 1 0 1 2 3
a = 2 0 2 4 6
a = 3 0 3 6 9

Why Are There So Many Bugs?

  • 3-bit numbers:
a × b b = 0 b = 1 b = 2 b = 3 b = 4 b = 5 b = 6 b = 7
a = 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
a = 1 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7
a = 2 0 2 4 6 8 10 12 14
a = 3 0 3 6 9 12 15 18 21
a = 4 0 4 8 12 16 20 24 28
a = 5 0 5 10 15 20 25 30 35
a = 6 0 6 12 18 24 30 36 42
a = 7 0 7 14 21 28 35 42 49

Why Are There So Many Bugs?

Some Ideas

Haphazard testing (or “just try it and see if it works”)

  • Not likely to find bugs
  • Only works if program is very buggy

Some Ideas

Random or statistical testing

  • Other engineering disciplines:
    • test 1% of hard drives and infer the defect rate
    • open fridge 1000 times in 24 hours
  • Doesn’t work well for software:
    • discontinuous and discrete across the input space

Putting on Your Testing Hat

When you’re coding:

  • your goal is to make the program work

When you’re testing:

  • you want to make it fail

Test-First Programming

  1. Specification
  2. Tests
  3. Actual code
def classify(x: float) -> str:
    """
    Classify a number as positive, zero, or negative.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : float
        The number to classify.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        - ``"positive"`` if x > 0
        - ``"zero"``     if x == 0
        - ``"negative"`` if x < 0

    Examples
    --------
    >>> classify(1)
    'positive'
    >>> classify(0)
    'zero'
    >>> classify(-3)
    'negative'
    >>> classify(float('inf'))
    'positive'
    >>> classify(float('-inf'))
    'negative'
    """

Choosing Test Cases by Partitioning



  • Trade-off:
    • test cases that are small and fast
    • test cases that are large enough to validate the program
  • Divide the input space into subdomains
  • Choose one test case from each subdomain

Example: max(a, b)




Partition Test case (a, b) Expected max(a, b)
\(a < b\) \((1, 2)\) \(2\)
\(a = b\) \((9, 9)\) \(9\)
\(a > b\) \((-5, -6)\) \(-5\)

Include Boundaries in the Partition

Boundary type Example Why bugs happen
zero 0 between positive and negative off-by-one: <= 0 instead of < 0
numeric limits sys.float_info.max, sys.float_info.min overflow to inf

Include Boundaries in the Partition

Boundary type Example Why bugs happen
empty collection "", [], np.array([]) special case: empty often skips loops or breaks indexing
first/last element list[0], list[-1] off-by-one: < vs <=, counter starting at 0 vs 1

Example: max(a, b)




Partition Test case (a, b) Expected max(a, b)
\(a < b\) \((1, 2)\) \(2\)
\(a = b\) \((9, 9)\) \(9\)
\(a > b\) \((-5, -6)\) \(-5\)
\(a = b\) \((0, 0)\) \(0\)
\(\infty > a\) \((\infty, -6)\) \(\infty\)

Covering the Partition

Strategy Description Example coverage
full Cartesian product every legal combination of all partition dimensions 5 parts × 5 parts = 25 test cases
cover each part every part of each dimension covered at least once 5 parts × 5 parts → as few as 5 test cases

Covering the Partition

Strategy Description Example coverage
compromise guided by human judgement, caution, and code coverage tools somewhere in between

Coverage Reports

Three common kinds of coverage:

  • Statement coverage: is every statement run by some test case?
  • Branch coverage: for every if or while statement in the program, are both the true and the false direction taken by some test case?
  • Path coverage: is every possible combination of branches—every path through the program—taken by some test case?

Black Box and Glass Box Testing

Black box testing

  • test cases only from the specification
  • partitioned without looking at the actual code
  • examples: our previous approach to test multiply and max

Glass box testing

  • test cases from actual implementation
  • example: implementation selects different algorithms depending on the input

Automated Testing

Source: xkcd

  • Regressing: introducing other bugs when you fix new bugs or add new features
  • Regression testing: running all your tests after every change

Automated Testing

Test-first debugging:

  1. Bug arises
  2. Write a test case for it that elicits it
  3. Add it to your test suite

Part 3: Unit Tests in Python

Module mymodule.py:

def classify(x: float) -> str:
    """Classify a number as positive, zero, or negative."""
    if x > 0:
        return "positive"
    elif x == 0:
        return "zero"
    else:
        return "negative"

Unit test test_mymodule.py:

from mymodule import classify

def test_positive():
    assert classify(1) == "positive"

def test_zero():
    assert classify(0) == "zero"

# test_negative is missing on purpose!

On the terminal:

pip install pytest pytest-cov
pytest test_mymodule.py --cov=mymodule --cov-report=html


Background:

Part Meaning
pytest run the test suite
test_mymodule.py only run tests in this file
--cov=mymodule measure coverage of mymodule.py
--cov-report=html write report as HTML in htmlcov/

Summary

Tasks:

  • Write tests before you write code
  • Choose test cases systematically by partitioning
  • Test each each module with unit test in isolation

Tools:

  • Use glass box testing and coverage for your test suite
  • Use automated testing to keep bugs away
